title: The document model registry is keyed by document type and version, with an absent version treated as 1, so two versions of one type coexist
content:
The registry holds document model modules keyed by **document type and version**, and the reactor reads it to resolve the reducer, utils and specification for a document when it executes a job. It also holds the **upgrade manifests** describing how to migrate a document up one version step.

Two details decide how lookups behave. The document type used as the key is `module.documentModel.global.id` — not a name or a package — and a module's version comes from its optional `version` field, which the registry **treats as `1` when absent**. So two different versions of the same type coexist happily, and an unversioned legacy module simply occupies slot 1.

`registerModules(...modules)` returns `RegistrationResult<DocumentModelModule>[]` — one per input, **in input order** — and **never throws**. A module whose `(documentType, version)` pair is already registered produces a `DuplicateModuleError` *in its result*, and invalid or duplicate modules are skipped without affecting the rest. The default in-memory implementation is `DocumentModelRegistry`; both it and the interface are exported from `@powerhousedao/reactor`.

The practical consequence for error handling is the next note's subject: because nothing throws, a registration failure is only visible if you read the results or the logs.
